summary: order-service p99 rose to ~5s because its INSERTs against the shared ledger-db hit statement timeouts. The fault originates in portfolio-service: deploy dep-5905 (v4.5.0, deployed 08:56) added a holdings P&L query filtering trades by account_id + executed_at with no index/migration, which Postgres runs as a Seq Scan over 48.2M rows. This drove ledger-db CPU from ~30% to ~96%, slow queries from ~1/min to ~140/min, and connections from ~62 to ~199 starting ~08:50-09:00, saturating the shared DB and cascading timeouts to order-service (whose own CPU/request rate stayed flat). The reported autovacuum config change (cfg-2903, 08:00) is a red herring: it cannot produce a sequential scan and predates onset by ~50 min with no effect. Remedy: index/optimize portfolio-service's new query or roll back dep-5905.

ranked_hypotheses.title: portfolio-service deploy introduced an unindexed full-table-scan query that saturated shared ledger-db
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-5905 (portfolio-service v4.5.0, 08:56) added a holdings P&L query filtering trades by account_id + executed_at without a supporting index. Postgres plans it as a sequential scan over 48M rows, driving ledger-db CPU to ~96% and slow queries to ~140/min, which causes order-service INSERTs into the shared ledger-db to hit statement timeouts and p99 to rise to ~5s.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5905 rolled out portfolio-service v4.5.0 with a new trades query and no migration/index
The new query runs as a Seq Scan on trades (48.2M rows) from application_name=portfolio-service, first seen 08:58:38
ledger-db CPU/slow-queries/connections spike from ~08:50-09:00 while both apps' CPU and request rates stay flat
order-service INSERT INTO orders statements against shared ledger-db time out, so p99 rises to ~5s

assumptions: The 08:58:38 Seq Scan is the exact query added by dep-5905 (logs align on time, filter columns and application_name)
No other unlogged workload caused the scan

ranked_hypotheses.title: Autovacuum config change on ledger-db caused the slowdown
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-2903 changed ledger-db autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor from 0.2 to 0.1 at 08:00; more aggressive autovacuum consumed I/O/CPU and starved other queries, causing timeouts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The config change at 08:00 precedes the onset by ~50 min without effect (CPU flat ~30% through 08:40), and autovacuum scale-factor cannot turn an indexed lookup into a Seq Scan on trades. The slow-query evidence names portfolio-service's new query, not autovacuum.

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db infrastructure failure / capacity saturation independent of any change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: ledger-db underlying capacity (IOPS/disk) degraded, causing slow queries and timeouts with no triggering release.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Onset coincides exactly with dep-5905 (08:56) and the first slow query names the new portfolio-service query specifically; no disk/IOPS metric alarm is present and CPU saturation is explained by an identifiable query.

assumptions: The 08:58:38 Seq Scan (application_name=portfolio-service) is the exact query introduced by dep-5905
ledger-db has no supporting index on trades(account_id, executed_at)
order-service latency/timeouts are caused solely by shared ledger-db saturation (no independent order-service fault)

timeline.event: cfg-2903: ledger-db autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2 -> 0.1 (no observable effect: CPU still ~30% through 08:40)
dep-5905 deploys portfolio-service v4.5.0 with a new trades query (account_id + executed_at), no migration; rollout complete 08:56:32
ledger-db logs first slow query: Seq Scan on trades (48,211,907 rows) from application_name=portfolio-service
portfolio-service logs first 'holdings P&L query took 7459ms'
ledger-db CPU (30%->96%), slow_queries_per_min (1->140) and connections (62->199) spike; order-service p99 rises to ~5.2s
order-service first ERROR: ledger-db statement timeout on INSERT INTO orders

recommended_actions.action: Roll back dep-5905 (portfolio-service v4.5.0) or disable the new holdings P&L query to immediately relieve ledger-db
recommended_actions.rationale: Removing the unindexed Seq Scan should return ledger-db CPU/slow-queries to baseline and clear order-service timeouts

recommended_actions.action: Add a composite index on trades(account_id, executed_at) and ship it via a migration, then re-deploy
recommended_actions.rationale: The new query filters on exactly these columns; an index converts the 48M-row Seq Scan into an index scan

recommended_actions.action: Add a query-review/perf gate (EXPLAIN on production-scale data) before deploys touch the shared ledger-db
recommended_actions.rationale: Same failure mode as past incident HIST-111; a review gate prevents recurrence

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT action the autovacuum config change as the cause; keep cfg-2903 but note it is unrelated
recommended_actions.rationale: Evidence shows the config change did not cause the scan or the saturation

data_gaps: No EXPLAIN plan / index metadata for the trades table was directly available; the Seq Scan is inferred from ledger-db 'slow query ... Seq Scan on trades' log lines rather than a schema/index dump.
No explicit metric tying ledger-db IOPS/disk to the event; infrastructure_failure for ledger-db cannot be fully excluded from metrics alone, though the query-level evidence points to the deploy.
No access to deployment rollback status change after 10:59 (whether rollback of dep-5905 was attempted) to confirm recovery.

findings.statement: ledger-db CPU rose from ~30% (steady 07:00-08:40) to ~96% from the 08:50 bucket onward (max 98.05).
ledger-db slow_queries_per_min rose from ~1/min (steady through 08:40) to ~140/min from the 08:50/09:00 buckets.
ledger-db connections_active rose from ~62 (steady) to ~190-199 from the 08:50 bucket onward.
order-service CPU stayed flat at ~40% throughout (07:00-10:50), so the latency is not caused by order-service's own compute load.
order-service db_pool_in_use doubled from ~14 to ~46 in the same 08:50-09:00 window, consistent with queries blocking on a saturated shared DB rather than an order-service change.
ledger-db is a shared Postgres used by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service.
No order-service deployment exists in the incident window; the only deployment across all services was dep-5905 (portfolio-service).

findings.statement: The only config change in the window was cfg-2903 on ledger-db: autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2 -> 0.1 ('More aggressive autovacuum') at 08:00:00.
Historical incident HIST-111 (2025-05-22) documents the same pattern: a new report query without an index caused full table scans on ledger-db, categorized as bad_deployment.

findings.statement: portfolio-service request_rate stayed flat (~570 req/s) across the window, and both portfolio-service and order-service CPU stayed flat, so this is not a traffic surge.
